status_summary: The administration has pursued elimination of selected entities and non-statutory functions rather than a review keyed to GAO-identified duplication or management layers. Executive Order 14210 (signed 2025-02-11) told agencies to prioritize large-scale reductions in force in offices performing functions not required by statute and to report within 30 days on which of their components are statutorily required and whether any should be eliminated or consolidated. Executive Orders 14217 (2025-02-19) and 14238 (2025-03-14) directed 11 named entities to eliminate non-statutory components and reduce statutory functions to the legal minimum, and EO 14217 also directed termination of six advisory committees and of the Presidential Management Fellows Program and told OPM to begin withdrawing the Federal Executive Board rules. A Wikipedia account says a district court ruled against the dismantling of one of those entities, the U.S. Institute of Peace, on 2025-05-19 and the D.C. Circuit stayed that ruling on 2025-06-27; an Associated Press report of 2026-10-01 says the appeal remains pending with the stay in place and argument set for November 2026. No Federal Register document on management layers or span of control was found, and OPM's 2026 staffing-plan guidance lists organizational restructuring as an efficiency option without addressing layers or duplicated functions. GAO's 16th annual duplication report (2026-05-12) identified 97 new matters, and no administration action keyed to it was found.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14210 (published 2025-02-14) sets a one-hire-for-every-four-departures plan, directs agencies to prepare large-scale reductions in force prioritizing offices that perform functions not required by law, and requires reports within 30 days on whether agencies or subcomponents are statutorily required and should be eliminated or consolidated. It does not mention management layers or duplicative functions.

Executive Order 14217 (published 2025-02-25) directs the Presidio Trust, Inter-American Foundation, U.S. African Development Foundation and U.S. Institute of Peace to eliminate non-statutory components and cut statutory functions to the legal minimum, directs termination of six advisory committees and of the Presidential Management Fellows Program, and directs OPM to begin withdrawing the Federal Executive Board rules.

Executive Order 14238 (published 2025-03-20) applies the same direction to seven more entities: the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service, U.S. Agency for Global Media, Woodrow Wilson Center, Institute of Museum and Library Services, U.S. Interagency Council on Homelessness, CDFI Fund and Minority Business Development Agency. It contains no language on duplication or consolidation.

According to Wikipedia, the D.C. Circuit stays a 2025-05-19 district court ruling that found the removal of the U.S. Institute of Peace board illegal and voided later staff firings and the building transfer; in September 2025 the appeal was held in abeyance pending Trump v. Slaughter.

GAO releases its 16th annual duplication report (GAO-26-108505), identifying 97 new matters for congressional consideration and recommendations for agencies; the GAO page does not describe any administration action keyed to them.

OPM issues governmentwide guidance on annual staffing plans under Executive Order 14356. Agencies are to base needs on mission and to evaluate efficiency through technology, process changes, organizational restructuring and the mix of contractors and employees. The release does not mention management layers or spans of control. The date comes from OPM's news release index.

title: Cut duplicated functions and management layers, starting with items GAO has identified
uncertainties: GAO's full annual report on fragmentation, overlap and duplication was not read (an earlier fetch was rate limited); GAO's summary page was read, so whether the administration acted on specific GAO recommendations was not checked. Federal Register queries for management layers, layers of management and span of control returned no documents, but internal agency memoranda are not published there, and no OMB or OPM reorganization memorandum was searched for directly. The district court ruling and stay for the U.S. Institute of Peace come from Wikipedia and a 2026-10-01 Associated Press report, not court records; Wikipedia also lists litigation over other eliminated entities (for example the Institute of Museum and Library Services) that was not verified. Executive Order 14217 was amended by a June 2026 order that was not examined. Workforce-size reductions are tracked in c03-06 and agency-specific reorganizations in their own chapters, so this record covers only the cross-government duplication and layers recommendation. OPM's staffing-plan release gives no date on the page; the date is from its news release index, and its reference to EO 14356 was not checked against the Federal Register.
